function_analysis: A hull coating must (F1) lower turbulent skin friction on a clean hull (at 10 m/s the viscous length nu/u_tau is about 3.8 um, so any texture or slip must act at the 1-100 um scale and be judged in viscous units); (F2) keep the hull hydraulically smooth over time, because fouling dominates in service (slime adds roughly +10-20 %, calcareous fouling +30-80 % frictional resistance), i.e. prevent settlement or make settled organisms detach under flow or light cleaning, without releasing biocides; (F3) survive several years of seawater immersion, UV at the waterline, abrasion (fenders, ice, cleaning), cathodic-protection potentials and hydrostatic pressure at 5-15 m draft; (F4) be applicable over 1e3-1e4 m2 at shipyard cost. F2 is usually worth more than F1; F1 concepts that are killed by fouling within weeks are worthless in practice.
mechanism_classes_considered: trapped_gas_or_liquid: pinned plastron (shear-free gas-water interface) with active gas replenishment
interfacial_slip: hydration layers and liquid-infused films (small slip lengths, mostly antifouling value)
flow_redirection: riblets tuned to s+ about 15
porous_transport: preferentially streamwise-permeable skins (virtual-origin offset like riblets)
graded_stiffness: low-modulus foul-release skins, compliant walls, graded interlayers for durability
other (roughness control): hydraulically smooth hard coats with grooming, surface renewal by controlled erosion
electrostatic_field: high-frequency AC fields in seawater to deter larval settlement without electrolysis

rejected: polymer release (Toms effect) - reservoir depletes in hours to days; wall heating - heat flux needed is about 100x the friction power saved; uniform blowing through a porous hull - intake momentum drag exceeds the friction saving
analogues_considered: Salvinia molesta floating fern: eggbeater hairs with hydrophilic tips pinning an air layer
Aphelocheirus water bug: permanent sub-um plastron (stable but slip length too small to matter)
Seagrass canopies and streamwise fibre bundles: anisotropic permeability
Dolphin and pilot whale skin: compliance, low modulus, epidermal sloughing every few hours
Mussel byssus thread: stiffness gradient from soft proximal to stiff distal end, removing interface stress singularities
Nacre brick-and-mortar platelets: tough, abrasion-resistant, smooth hard composite
Fish mucus: hydrated glycoprotein layer resisting settlement
Weakly electric fish (Gymnotiformes): continuous low-amplitude AC fields in water
Technology: self-polishing copolymers (without biocide), glass-flake vinyl-ester hard coats with in-water grooming, impressed-current cathodic protection, electrolytic plastron restoration

candidates.title: Air-fed Salvinia plastron with hydrophilic-tip pinning
candidates.summary: A silicone mat of 300 um pitch eggbeater-type hairs whose hydrophilic tips pin a 0.5 mm air layer; a microporous base membrane connected to a low-pressure air manifold replaces gas lost by diffusion into the undersaturated water at draft depth. The shear-free interface gives a large slip length; the air feed removes the main reason passive plastrons fail on ships.

back_of_envelope.quantity: turbulent skin-friction reduction vs clean smooth hull at 10 m/s
back_of_envelope.formula: posts: b = L*(0.325/sqrt(phi_s) - 0.44) = 3e-4*(0.325/0.316-0.44) = 1.8e-4 m, b+ = b/(nu/u_tau) = 1.8e-4/3.8e-6 = 47; surfactants and meniscus deformation in seawater cut the effective log-law shift to dU+ about 3.5; Cf/Cf0 = (U0+/(U0+ + dU+))^2 = (31.6/35.1)^2 = 0.81

candidates.main_risk: Surfactants and biofilm immobilise the air-water interface and colonise the hairs within weeks, so the interface stops being shear-free and the layer is lost in waves and slamming.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest: Salvinia-effect air-retaining coatings (Barthlott, AirCoat) and ship air lubrication. New: the air layer is fed through a microporous base membrane at about 1 mL/(m2 s) to balance diffusive loss at draft depth, so the concept does not rely on a passive plastron surviving months.
candidates.inspiration_source: Salvinia molesta eggbeater hairs with hydrophilic terminal cells
candidates.physical_mechanism: The pinned gas layer replaces the no-slip wall by a mostly shear-free interface (solid fraction 0.1). In a channel or Couette model this is a Navier slip condition with slip length b from the post geometry and the gas layer viscosity; turbulent drag falls because the near-wall velocity profile is shifted upward. Laplace pressure 2*gamma/L = 480 Pa exceeds turbulent wall-pressure fluctuations (about 2.5*tau_w = 250 Pa); hydrostatic compression is handled by the air feed.

parameters.name: hair_pitch
parameters.justification: Salvinia hair spacing is 0.3-0.6 mm; smaller pitch raises Laplace stability, larger pitch raises slip

parameters.name: solid_area_fraction
parameters.justification: Wetted tip area fraction of the pinned hydrophilic tips

parameters.name: air_layer_thickness
parameters.justification: Hair height of engineered Salvinia replicas

parameters.name: air_supply_rate
parameters.justification: Diffusive gas loss at 10 m depth: k_m about 1.6e-4 m/s times N2 undersaturation about 0.5 mol/m3, as volume at 2 bar

candidates.title: Streamwise-permeable micro-channel skin (seagrass canopy analogue)
candidates.summary: A 100 um thick skin of streamwise micro-channels under a perforated top sheet: high streamwise permeability, very low spanwise and wall-normal permeability. Like riblets, it moves the virtual origin of the streamwise flow below that of the cross flow and so damps near-wall streamwise vortices, without protruding ridges that wear or trap slime at the tips.

back_of_envelope.quantity: turbulent skin-friction reduction vs clean smooth hull at 10 m/s
back_of_envelope.formula: dU+ about sqrt(Kx)+ - sqrt(Kz)+ (Gomez-de-Segura and Garcia-Mayoral 2019): sqrt(8e-11)/3.8e-6 = 2.35, sqrt(2e-12)/3.8e-6 = 0.37, dU+ about 2.0 ideal, about 1.4 after Kelvin-Helmholtz onset and manufacturing limits; Cf/Cf0 = (31.6/33.0)^2 = 0.92

candidates.main_risk: Biofilm and sediment clog the sub-surface channels within weeks, turning the skin into an ordinary rough wall.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest: riblets and DNS studies of anisotropic permeable substrates. New: a manufacturable channel-under-perforated-sheet design that reaches high Kx/Kz anisotropy (aligned fibre mats only reach about 2), for ship hulls, with a low-modulus silicone matrix to help fouling release.
candidates.inspiration_source: Streamwise-aligned seagrass (Posidonia) canopies and fibre bundles, plus DNS of preferentially permeable walls
candidates.physical_mechanism: Brinkman/Darcy flow in the skin coupled to the outer flow through a Beavers-Joseph type slip; the streamwise slip length is about sqrt(Kx) and the spanwise about sqrt(Kz). In a steady 1D model: channel flow over a Brinkman layer, giving the wall-shear change for given Kx and layer thickness.

parameters.name: streamwise_permeability
parameters.justification: sqrt(Kx)+ about 2-3 at viscous length 3.8 um

parameters.name: spanwise_permeability
parameters.justification: Channels are separated spanwise; only the perforated sheet connects them

parameters.name: wall_normal_permeability
parameters.justification: sqrt(Ky)+ below about 0.4 to avoid spanwise Kelvin-Helmholtz rollers

parameters.name: layer_thickness
parameters.justification: Several channel diameters deep so the Darcy regime is reached

candidates.title: Low-modulus silicone riblets with foul-release skin
candidates.summary: Trapezoidal riblets of 60 um spacing moulded in a 1 MPa fluorosilicone, so the same layer reduces clean-hull friction and lets settled organisms detach under flow. The riblets are sized for s+ about 16 at cruise speed.

back_of_envelope.quantity: turbulent skin-friction reduction vs clean smooth hull
back_of_envelope.formula: s+ = 6e-5/3.8e-6 = 16 (near optimum); lab dU+ about 1.4, hull-averaged over speed and position about 1.0; Cf/Cf0 = (31.6/32.6)^2 = 0.94; minus tip rounding

candidates.main_risk: A 10-30 um slime layer fills the grooves within weeks at low speed, removing the riblet effect.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest: shark-skin riblet films and riblet paints; heavily adapted in that the riblets are made of foul-release silicone (low E, low surface energy) rather than rigid polymer, combining F1 and F2 in one layer. Still textbook-adjacent.
candidates.physical_mechanism: Riblets create a longitudinal protrusion height larger than the transverse one, shifting quasi-streamwise vortices away from the wall. Modelled as longitudinal Stokes flow in a riblet cross-section (2D Poisson problem) giving the protrusion heights.

parameters.name: riblet_spacing
parameters.justification: s+ about 16 at viscous length 3.8 um

parameters.name: silicone_youngs_modulus
parameters.justification: Foul-release silicones are 0.3-3 MPa; deformation under 100 Pa shear is negligible

candidates.title: Graded-modulus foul-release laminate (whale-skin analogue)
candidates.summary: A three-layer coating: epoxy anticorrosive base, a 5 MPa silicone mid layer, and a 150 um skin of 0.5 MPa silicone with low surface energy. Hard fouling detaches at a small fraction of the stress needed on a rigid paint because the soft layer lets cracks initiate at low load, and the mid layer protects the skin against cuts.

back_of_envelope.quantity: critical detachment stress of a barnacle base vs rigid epoxy paint
back_of_envelope.formula: thin-film fracture scaling sigma_c ~ sqrt(w*E/t): epoxy sqrt(0.1*3e9/3e-4) = 1.0 MPa (matches measured about 1 MPa); soft skin sqrt(0.05*1e6/4e-4) = 0.011 MPa; measured foul-release coatings reach 0.05-0.15 MPa because cement interlocks, so take 85 %

candidates.main_risk: Hard fouling only self-cleans above about 15 kn; slow or idle ships still foul and need cleaning, which cuts the soft skin.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest: commercial silicone foul-release coatings (Intersleek, Hempasil). New: a deliberate modulus gradient rather than a tie-coat, so release performance and cut resistance are traded explicitly. Moderate novelty.
candidates.inspiration_source: Low-modulus, graded dermis of dolphins and pilot whales
candidates.physical_mechanism: Detachment of a rigid disc bonded to a thin elastic layer: the energy release rate grows with load^2*t/E, so crack initiation stress falls as sqrt(w*E/t). A 1D layered elasticity model gives the interfacial stress under a pulled base.

parameters.name: top_layer_thickness
parameters.justification: Thick enough for the fracture scaling, thin enough for cost

candidates.title: Byssus-graded tie zone between epoxy and silicone
candidates.summary: Instead of a thin tie-coat, a 60 um zone whose modulus falls continuously from 3 GPa to 1 MPa (graded filler content), copying the stiffness gradient of the mussel byssal thread. It removes the bimaterial stress singularity at cut edges and damaged spots, which is where silicone foul-release coatings start to peel.

back_of_envelope.quantity: peak interfacial stress at a coating edge under fender shear vs abrupt tie-coat
back_of_envelope.formula: a simple shear-lag model shows almost no change because the silicone's own shear compliance t/G = 3e-4/3.3e5 = 9e-10 m/Pa dominates the tie layer (2e-14); the gain comes from removing the edge singularity (Dundurs mismatch alpha about 1 for an abrupt joint -> 0 for a graded one); finite-element results for graded joints show about 2x lower peak stress

candidates.main_risk: Peeling of real coatings is set by chemical bond strength and damage from cleaning, not by the elastic edge stress, so the gradient may not extend coating life.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest: silicone tie-coats and functionally graded coatings in general. New: a byssus-like modulus gradient used specifically to make foul-release silicones last longer. Low to moderate novelty.
candidates.inspiration_source: Mussel byssal thread (stiff distal, soft proximal, graded collagen-histidine domains)
candidates.physical_mechanism: Stress transfer across a graded interlayer: a 1D elastic model through the thickness with position-dependent modulus E(y), loaded by shear at the free edge, gives the peak interfacial stress for abrupt and graded profiles.

parameters.name: graded_zone_thickness
parameters.justification: Byssus gradient spans a few percent of thread length; scaled to film build

parameters.name: edge_shear_load
parameters.justification: Fender rubbing and cleaning brush contact stresses

candidates.title: Dolphin-type compliant skin tuned to cruise speed
candidates.summary: A 3 mm viscoelastic gel layer whose shear wave speed is about half the cruise speed, the regime in which compliant walls have shown small turbulent drag reductions in water. The same very soft layer acts as a foul-release surface.

back_of_envelope.quantity: turbulent skin-friction reduction vs rigid smooth hull
back_of_envelope.formula: c_t = sqrt(G/rho) = sqrt(2.5e4/1000) = 5 m/s = 0.5*U; experiments at matched c_t/U (Choi et al. 1997, Kramer) report 0-7 %; take the lower half

candidates.main_risk: Off design speed, or above the divergence threshold, the wall forms static waves that increase drag, and a 25 kPa gel tears in service.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest: Kramer's compliant coatings and dolphin-skin studies. Little new beyond combining with foul-release; the drag effect is disputed.
candidates.physical_mechanism: Wall compliance damps near-wall velocity fluctuations. A steady model can only express it as an effective slip or modified near-wall viscosity, which is a weak representation.

parameters.name: shear_modulus
parameters.justification: Gives shear wave speed about 0.5*U at 10 m/s

candidates.title: Nacre-architected glass-flake hard coat with in-water grooming
candidates.summary: A biocide-free, brick-and-mortar coating of aligned glass flakes in vinyl-ester that stays hydraulically smooth (average hull roughness about 40 um) for 10+ years and survives frequent soft robotic grooming. It saves friction by staying smoother than conventional paint systems, and fouling is handled by grooming, not chemistry.

back_of_envelope.quantity: frictional resistance reduction vs a conventional new paint system (AHR 125 um), 200 m ship at 15 kn

candidates.main_risk: Without frequent grooming (every 2-6 weeks) the hard surface fouls like any inert surface, and operators do not keep the schedule.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest: glass-flake hard coatings with hull grooming (e.g. Ecospeed-type systems). New: platelet alignment designed nacre-like for toughness and smoothness retention under grooming. Low novelty but high durability and zero biocide.
candidates.physical_mechanism: Friction of a turbulent boundary layer over a rough wall: equivalent sand roughness k_s maps to a roughness function dU+(k_s+); keeping k_s+ below about 5 keeps the wall hydraulically smooth. Can be modelled as a wall-law offset or effective negative slip.

parameters.name: coating_hull_roughness
parameters.justification: Achievable AHR of a sprayed hard coat

candidates.title: Self-sloughing multilayer hydrogel epidermis
candidates.summary: A stack of 5 um layers of hydrolysable polyester, each with weak interlayer bonds, erodes about 30 um per year by surface hydrolysis without biocides. Like the pilot whale epidermis, the surface is renewed continuously, so soft fouling loses its anchor and the hull stays at a light-slime level instead of heavy fouling.

back_of_envelope.quantity: frictional resistance reduction vs an uncoated, fouled hull after 12 months
back_of_envelope.formula: Schultz 2007 powering penalties at 15 kn: heavy slime about +18 %, light slime about +9 %; renewal keeps light slime vs heavy slime on inert paint: 1 - 1.09/1.18 = 7.6 %; some small calcareous avoided -> about 10 %

candidates.main_risk: An erosion rate of 30 um per year is far slower than the hours it takes barnacle cyprids to cement, so without biocides the surface renewal does not stop hard fouling.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest: biocide-free self-polishing copolymers. New: discrete weakly bonded 5 um sheets (sloughing rather than smooth polishing). Moderate novelty, weak evidence.
candidates.inspiration_source: Pilot whale and dolphin epidermal sloughing
candidates.physical_mechanism: Water diffuses into the top layer and hydrolyses it; in the frame moving with the eroding surface this is a steady 1D reaction-diffusion problem D*c'' + v*c' - k*c = 0 whose penetration depth sqrt(D/k) sets surface erosion and the renewal rate. The drag effect is indirect (roughness growth avoided).

parameters.name: total_thickness
parameters.justification: About 9 years at the design erosion rate

parameters.name: hydrolysis_rate_constant
parameters.justification: Gives a penetration depth sqrt(D/k) of about 30 um

candidates.title: Electric-fish-type high-frequency AC settlement deterrent
candidates.summary: Interdigitated carbon or titanium electrodes at 0.5 mm pitch under a thin porous topcoat drive a 10 kHz field of about 10 V/m in the first 0.2 mm of seawater. At this frequency the double layer carries the current capacitively, so there is no electrolysis and no chlorine, while the field may deter settling larvae and diatoms.

back_of_envelope.quantity: frictional resistance reduction vs uncoated fouled hull after 12 months (speculative, depends on biological threshold)
back_of_envelope.formula: power: sigma*E^2*(pitch/pi) = 5*100*1.6e-4 = 0.08 W/m2; double-layer drop at J = 50 A/m2: J/(2*pi*f*C) = 50/(2*pi*1e4*0.2) = 4 mV, far below 1.2 V; if settlement falls to a light-slime level: 1 - 1.09/1.18 = 7.6 %

candidates.main_risk: There is little evidence that a non-Faradaic field of about 10 V/m deters barnacle cyprids or diatoms; the biological threshold may be 10-100x higher, making power and electrode erosion prohibitive.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest: electrochemical and pulsed-DC antifouling, which works mostly by electrochlorination. New: purely capacitive high-frequency AC to avoid chlorine. Physically sound; biologically unproven.
candidates.inspiration_source: Continuous electric organ discharge of weakly electric fish
candidates.physical_mechanism: Quasi-static potential in a conductor above interdigitated electrodes: Laplace equation on a rectangle (one electrode period by several pitches height) with alternating potentials at the bottom; the field decays as exp(-pi*y/pitch). The evaluator computes the field strength at the surface and the fraction of area above the threshold.

parameters.name: electrode_pitch
parameters.justification: Sets field penetration depth pitch/pi = 0.16 mm

parameters.name: drive_frequency
parameters.justification: High enough to stay capacitive at the double layer

parameters.name: target_field_strength
parameters.justification: Order of magnitude of fields near weakly electric fish

parameters.name: applied_voltage_amplitude
parameters.justification: V; about E*pitch/2 plus double-layer drop
